content: Screening for diabetic retinopathy should be performed at the time of diagnosis of diabetes and subsequently on an annual basis. Optimizing glycemic control is essential to slow the progression of diabetic retinopathy. For patients with stable retinopathy and who are meeting glycemic targets, less frequent screening, such as every two years, may be considered. The use of retinal photography is recommended to enhance the effectiveness of screening and to improve access to diabetic retinopathy screening services.
